claims.text: Worked example: 90 requests at 5 ms and 10 at 500 ms average 54.5 ms (about 55; section 6 says about 50) while nobody waited near that; sorted, the 95th request is a 500 ms one, so p95 = 500 ms, about ten times the average.
The p95 (95th percentile) is the value that 95% of observations are at or below (the time 95% of requests took at most).

A Prometheus histogram exposes cumulative counters <basename>_bucket{le="<upper bound>"} (each counts observations <= le, so each includes the smaller buckets, le="+Inf" counts all), plus <basename>_sum and <basename>_count.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Metric types (Histogram); Histograms and summaries

claims.text: prometheus-net's UseHttpMetrics records http_request_duration_seconds as a histogram with the same labels as the request counter (code, method, controller, action, endpoint).

claims.text: histogram_quantile(phi, b) estimates the phi-quantile from buckets that keep le (hence sum by (le) after rate): target rank phi times the +Inf count, first bucket reaching it, interpolated inside; precision depends on bucket bounds; the result has no le label.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Query functions, histogram_quantile(); Histograms and summaries (errors of quantile estimation)

claims.text: The average duration over a window is rate(_sum[5m]) / rate(_count[5m]) (summed over series with sum(...) on both sides); dividing the raw _sum by _count gives the average since the process started.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Histograms and summaries (average request duration from _sum and _count)

claims.text: Both queries return one result with no labels ({}): sum(...) without by aggregates everything; in the first, sum by (le) keeps only le, which histogram_quantile consumes.

promql-latency.sh@stage-2 lines 14-28: 20 GET /api/v1/products/1, prints _sum, _count and 17 _bucket lines of the code=200 histogram with labels cut to {..., sleeps 11 s (two scrapes), queries p95 and average; endpoint label is the route template api/v1/products/{id:int}.
Neither the API nor Prometheus keeps individual request durations for this metric: only per-bucket counts, _sum and _count are exposed and stored.
